name: CKA Node & Component Troubleshooting
description: Hands-on node-level operations you can't practice in CK-X: bring a NotReady node back, repair a crash-looping control-plane component, uncordon/cordon/drain nodes, run a static pod on the control-plane, and schedule a tolerating pod onto a tainted node.
objective: CKA › Troubleshooting (30%). Prove you can recover a cluster: NotReady nodes, broken components, uncordon, static pods, drain, and taints.

questions.title: Recover a NotReady node
questions.prompt:
Worker node `$W1` (run `kindlab up` to see node names — e.g. `kindlab-worker`) shows **NotReady** — its kubelet has stopped.

Bring the node back so it reports **Ready** again.

_Hint:_ `docker exec -it $W1 bash`, then restart the kubelet with `systemctl start kubelet` (check status with `systemctl status kubelet`). The node returns to `Ready` within ~15s.

questions.title: Repair the kube-controller-manager
questions.prompt:
The **kube-controller-manager** is down — a bad flag was added to its static pod manifest on the control-plane node, so it crash-loops.

Find and fix it (the manifest is `/etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-controller-manager.yaml` on `$CP`) so the component becomes healthy again.

_Hint:_ `docker exec -it $CP bash`, inspect the manifest, remove the bogus flag; the kubelet restarts the static pod automatically within ~15s.

verification.description: kube-controller-manager static pod is Ready again

questions.title: Uncordon a node
questions.prompt:
Node `$W1` was cordoned during earlier maintenance and is still **unschedulable**. Bring it back into service so the scheduler can place pods on it again.

_Hint:_ `kubectl uncordon $W1` clears `spec.unschedulable`.

questions.title: Static pod on the control-plane
questions.prompt:
On the control-plane node `$CP`, create a **static pod** named `cp-web` using image `nginx:alpine` by placing a manifest in `/etc/kubernetes/manifests/` on that node.

The kubelet will create a read-only **mirror pod** named `cp-web-$CP` in the `default` namespace. Verify it is Running.

_Hint:_ `docker exec -it $CP bash`, then write the manifest; the pod name in the manifest should be `cp-web`.

questions.title: Drain a node
questions.prompt:
A Deployment named `draintest` (3 replicas) is running in the `default` namespace. Node `$W2` needs maintenance.

**Drain** `$W2`, ignoring DaemonSets, so that all `draintest` pods are evicted from it and it becomes unschedulable.

_Hint:_ `kubectl drain $W2 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data`. Drain cordons the node first, then evicts the workloads; the Deployment reschedules them onto other nodes.

questions.title: Taint a node and schedule a tolerating pod
questions.prompt:
Reserve node `$W1` for batch workloads.

1. Add the taint `workload=batch:NoSchedule` to node `$W1`.
2. Create a pod named `batch` in the `default` namespace using image `busybox:1.36` running `sleep 3600`, that **tolerates** this taint and is scheduled onto `$W1`.

_Hint:_ `kubectl taint nodes $W1 workload=batch:NoSchedule`, then give the pod a matching toleration (key `workload`, value `batch`, effect `NoSchedule`) and pin it to `$W1` with `nodeName` or a nodeSelector.
